checklist.task: Validate local demand and supply in your target county
checklist.instructions: DHSR publishes separate Adult Care Home and Family Care Home listings (updated 07/30/2026, XLSX). Download them and count licensed homes and beds in your county. NCDHHS reports more than 1,200 adult care homes statewide. The 65+ population is about 2.04 million (18%) in 2025, projected to reach about 3.0 million by 2050, and the 85+ population is projected to grow from about 186,000 to about 510,000. County-level occupancy and waitlist data are not published in the sources reviewed, so call local homes, hospital discharge planners and county DSS.
checklist.cite: DHSR Licensed Facilities listings; NC DHHS Insights Into Aging

checklist.task: Read the NC DHSR overview of adult care home regulation and the licensing pages for your category
checklist.instructions: Read the ACLS overview page, the 'License an Adult Care Home' page and the 'License a Family Care Home' page in full before spending money. Note that several quotes in this bundle came from search excerpts, so recheck them on the live pages. Free; about 2 hours.

checklist.task: Form your legal entity (NC LLC)
checklist.instructions: File Articles of Organization with the NC Secretary of State. A secondary source puts the fee at $125 online or by mail. Use the exact entity name on every DHSR, county, NCTracks and insurance filing, because the licensee named on the application is the entity that holds the license.

checklist.task: Obtain an EIN and open a business bank account
checklist.instructions: Apply for an EIN online at irs.gov. You need it for payroll, the bank account, NC DES registration and NCTracks. Keep operating funds separate from personal funds from day one.

checklist.task: Calendar the NC LLC annual report
checklist.instructions: The annual report is due April 15 every year after the year of formation. Secondary sources citing the Secretary of State put the fee at $200 on paper or $203 online by card. An LLC ordinarily becomes eligible for administrative dissolution when the report is 60 days late, followed by notice and a 60-day cure period. Reinstatement costs $100 (secondary source). Confirm amounts on sosnc.gov.
checklist.cite: NC Secretary of State (via Ezel / State Business Compliance)

checklist.task: Confirm entity-level tax and local business license obligations with a CPA
checklist.instructions: Whether NC franchise tax applies to your operating entity was not verified. City and county business license fees (Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro and others) were not researched. Ask your CPA and your city/county clerk, and replace the $0 franchise-tax placeholder in the P&L with the confirmed figure.

checklist.task: Engage a healthcare attorney and an accountant familiar with adult care homes
checklist.instructions: Have the attorney review the lease or purchase contract, resident admission agreements, and any CON or acquisition documents. Have the accountant set up the chart of accounts and the Adult Care Cost Report process (see Phase 8). Budget for this in the P&L; the model carries $400/month for accounting, payroll service and legal as an operator estimate.

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Confirm that new ACH beds require a Certificate of Need (CON)
checklist.instructions: DHSR states that no one may develop new adult care home beds without a CON. All CON requirements must be met before the license application is submitted for a facility not yet licensed. Call the CON Section at 919-855-3873 to confirm your plan.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License an ACH; 10A NCAC 13F .0204

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Check whether your county has a scheduled CON review and a bed need determination
checklist.instructions: CON applications are accepted only for proposed beds in a county where DHSR has scheduled a review. The 2026 State Medical Facilities Plan (effective January 1, 2026) governs need. A secondary source says the Proposed 2026 SMFP listed need determinations only in Halifax and Perquimans counties. That is a proposed-plan statement, not a confirmed final need number. Check the final SMFP and the CON Section's review schedule for your county.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License an ACH; 2026 SMFP

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Review SMFP Policy LTC-3 (Certification of Beds for Special Assistance)
checklist.instructions: The 2026 SMFP includes this policy for CON applicants proposing new beds under a need determination. Read it before drafting an application and decide how many beds you will certify for SA.

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Prepare and file the CON application and plan for the 150-day decision window
checklist.instructions: A decision to approve or disapprove is made within 150 days of the beginning of the designated review period. The CON application fee amount was not found in the sources reviewed, so request it from the CON Section (919-855-3873). Budget for consultants and legal support; this cost is not in the P&L.

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Alternative route: evaluate buying an existing licensed home instead of seeking a CON
checklist.instructions: The practical alternative to a CON is acquiring an existing licensed home. A licensee selling a home must give written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents at least 30 days before the planned change of licensee. Ask ACLS exactly what the incoming licensee must file. The licensed capacity of an ACH must comply with the CON issued to the facility, so confirm the seller's licensed bed count and CON status in diligence.

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Benchmark capital scale against recent CON filings
checklist.instructions: One example: a CON application to relocate 64 memory-care beds to develop The Landings of New Hanover in Wilmington was reported at $12.9 million with completion expected in October 2030. This is a secondary news source and the project is much larger than the models here. Use it only to understand how long and how capital-intensive new-bed development can be.

checklist.phase: PHASE 3 — CERTIFICATE OF NEED & ENTRY ROUTE (ACH)
checklist.task: Family care homes (2–6 beds): ask ACLS whether CON applies and confirm your entry point
checklist.instructions: The sources reviewed cover CON for adult care home beds only. Whether CON applies to 2–6 bed family care homes was not verified. Initial contact for an FCH should be made with the adult services section of your local county DSS. Ask the adult home specialist directly and confirm in writing.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License a Family Care Home

checklist.task: Obtain local zoning approval for the site before committing to a lease or purchase
checklist.instructions: An adult care home must be in a location approved by local zoning boards. For FCHs, the county adult home specialist verifies that the location is approved by the local zoning office before proceeding. Distance, density and use-classification rules were not researched, so call the planning department of the city or county with the specific address.
checklist.cite: 10A NCAC 13F; DHSR ACLS License a Family Care Home

checklist.task: Identify the NC State Building Code section that applies to your resident count
checklist.instructions: FCHs with four to six residents must meet the NC State Building Code Licensed Residential Care Facilities section. Facilities with seven to twelve residents must meet the Large Residential Care Facilities section. Facilities housing 13 or more residents must meet I-2 Institutional occupancy for new construction and renovations. The I-2 requirement raises capital cost, so price it before choosing a 13+ bed building.
checklist.cite: 10A NCAC 13G; 10A NCAC 13F; DHSR ACLS Facility Licensure Information

checklist.task: Submit plans to the DHSR Construction Section and pay the plan-review invoice
checklist.instructions: Construction plan review is invoiced by DHSR, and projects are not reviewed until the invoice is paid in full. The review fee amount is not stated on the pages reviewed, so ask the Construction Section (919-855-3893) for it and add it to your startup budget. Applies to new or renovated homes.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License an Adult Care Home

checklist.task: Schedule the local fire marshal inspection and obtain sanitation and occupancy approvals
checklist.instructions: The ACH application requires an approved fire and building safety inspection report from the local fire marshal, submitted upon completion of construction or renovation. Sanitation and occupancy approvals are also part of the packet. Contact the local fire marshal and the county environmental health office early; approvals can delay your application.

checklist.task: Get contractor quotes for fire, sprinkler, alarm and accessibility upgrades
checklist.instructions: The model carries $5,000–$60,000 for fire and life-safety upgrades and $5,000–$50,000 for accessibility and physical-plant upgrades. Both are operator estimates. Get written quotes from a licensed fire-protection contractor and a general contractor, and replace the estimates.
checklist.cite: Operator estimate; DHSR Facility Licensure Information

checklist.task: Confirm the status of any 2026 physical-plant rule readoption before finalizing design
checklist.instructions: The status of 10A NCAC 13F/13G physical-plant rule readoption was not verified. Check the ACLS announcements page and the DHSR rules page for the version in effect on your application date.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS Announcements; DHSR rules page

checklist.task: Negotiate the lease or purchase with licensing contingencies
checklist.instructions: The model carries rent as a fixed cost from day one at $600 per licensed bed per month, which is an operator estimate (no NC rent benchmark was retrieved). Make the lease contingent on zoning approval, CON (ACH), plan review and fire marshal approval. Vacant beds still cost rent, so negotiate a free-rent or reduced-rent period during licensing.

checklist.task: Confirm the administrator meets certification requirements (ACH)
checklist.instructions: ACH administrators must meet the certification criteria under G.S. 90-288.14, and the applicant must be at least 21. Certification qualifies on education, or on supervisory experience: a minimum of 60 months of supervisory experience, or a combination of education and experience. Check the ACLS Administrator Certification page for the exact education and experience combinations.

checklist.task: Complete the 120-hour Administrator-in-Training (AIT) program
checklist.instructions: The program consists of at least 20 hours of coursework or study and at least 100 hours of on-the-job training. Allow roughly 3 or more weeks of full-time work, depending on your schedule. The AIT program cost is not stated in the sources reviewed and is not in the startup budget.

checklist.task: Submit the criminal background check for the administrator applicant
checklist.instructions: The SBI criminal history fee is $14, or $38 if a federal FBI report is also required. Pay DHSR by money order or cashier's check. State results take about 2 weeks. The FBI check can take up to 12 weeks for NC residents under five years, so start this early.
checklist.cite: ACLS Administrator Certification Guidelines; DHSR ACLS License a Family Care Home

checklist.task: Register for and pass the administrator exam (online testing)
checklist.instructions: The exam fee stays at $50. DHSR announced that starting September 25, 2026 it no longer accepts paper applications and payments for administrator testing, and testing moves online. The announcement was found on a test.ncdhhs.gov mirror, so confirm the current process on the production ACLS forms page.

checklist.task: Family care homes: obtain administrator approval and confirm its training requirements
checklist.instructions: FCH administrators receive an approval, not certification, and there is no fee to renew it. The FCH administrator training-hour requirements under 10A NCAC 13G were not verified, so ask the county adult home specialist or ACLS for the current requirements before you enroll in any course.

checklist.task: Designate a qualified manager to run the home when the administrator is absent
checklist.instructions: A manager must be at least 21 and hold a high school diploma or GED, and must earn 12 hours of continuing education a year on adult care home management or care of the elderly and disabled. DHSR replaced the 'Administrator in Charge' title with 'Manager' in the readopted staffing rules effective September 1, 2024. In 7–12 bed homes the administrator or manager must be in the facility or within 500 feet with two-way telecommunication at all times.
checklist.cite: ACLS Joint Training May 2025 — Staffing of Licensed Adult Care Homes

checklist.task: Plan administrator renewal and continuing education
checklist.instructions: Certified administrators renew with a $30 non-refundable fee (electronic check or debit card) and must complete 30 CE hours every two years after the first renewal. Put the renewal date on your compliance calendar.

checklist.task: Ask ACLS about background-check requirements for owners, principals and affiliates
checklist.instructions: Only administrator-applicant checks were verified in this research. Ask ACLS whether owners or other principals must also be checked, and what the cost and timeline are.

checklist.task: Family care home: contact your county DSS adult home specialist to start the packet
checklist.instructions: FCH applicants do not apply directly to ACLS; they start with the adult services section of the local county DSS. The specialist verifies local zoning approval before construction review proceeds and submits the packet to ACLS.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License a Family Care Home

checklist.task: Family care home: submit the initial licensure fee
checklist.instructions: The FCH initial licensure fee is $350, submitted by the county adult home specialist with the packet. Confirm the payment method with your specialist.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License a Family Care Home

checklist.task: Adult care home: assemble the initial application (DHSR/AC 4603) packet
checklist.instructions: The application materials include the initial license application, a bed capacity statement, plans, the construction review fee, and the fire, sanitation and occupancy approvals at completion. The initial application and fee are submitted to ACLS in Raleigh only after the construction review steps are complete. The initial fee must accompany the application.

checklist.task: Adult care home: confirm which initial fee governs before you pay
checklist.instructions: The DHSR licensing page lists a non-refundable initial fee of $400 plus $19 per bed (12 beds = $628; 20 beds = $780). The G.S. 131D-2.5 schedule quoted on DHSR forms gives $360 + $17.50 per bed annually for homes over six beds. The two conflict and the conflict is unresolved. The model uses the higher figure. Ask ACLS to confirm the exact amount in writing before you submit payment.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License an Adult Care Home; G.S. 131D-2.5 as quoted on DHSR forms

checklist.task: Make sure CON requirements are met and bed capacity matches the CON before submitting (ACH)
checklist.instructions: Before submitting a license application for a facility not yet licensed, all CON requirements must be met under G.S. 131E, Article 9. The facility's bed capacity and services must comply with the CON issued to the facility. Attach your CON documents to the packet.

checklist.task: Prepare for the pre-licensing survey and the 14-day decision notice
checklist.instructions: ACLS conducts a pre-licensing survey to confirm compliance. ACLS must notify the applicant and the county DSS in writing within 14 days from the decision to license or not to license. Have policies, staffing records, administrator documentation and the building ready before the survey.

checklist.task: Understand the six-month initial license and the follow-up survey
checklist.instructions: Initial licenses are issued for a six-month period, after which ACLS must inspect or survey the home. For family care homes, a survey is conducted around four months after the initial license is issued, and it is needed before a full license is granted. Plan your admissions and staffing so the home is compliant from the first day it opens.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License an ACH; DHSR ACLS License an FCH

checklist.task: Ask ACLS when you may admit your first resident
checklist.instructions: The rule text on when admissions may begin was not captured in the sources reviewed. Confirm with ACLS in writing that the license has been issued before you admit anyone, and do not market a start date that depends on licensing until the decision notice arrives.

checklist.task: Build a staffing plan that meets the staffing rules for your census
checklist.instructions: ACHs with 7–20 residents must have at least one designated staff member per shift to provide personal care services and supervision. For a census of 21–40 residents, 16 aide duty hours are required on first and second shifts (third-shift hours vary by census). Facilities with 31 or more residents must employ a Personal Care Aide Supervisor. Homes with 81 or more residents need an administrator on duty at least eight hours per day, five days per week. Questions go to DHSR.AdultCare.Questions@dhhs.nc.gov.
checklist.cite: ACLS Joint Training May 2025 — Staffing of Licensed Adult Care Homes

checklist.task: Staff for awake overnight coverage if any resident is disoriented or wanders
checklist.instructions: In homes with 7–12 residents, if any resident is disoriented or has wandering behavior, at least one staff member must be on duty and awake at all times. The models carry 730 hours a month (24/7) of aide coverage for the 6- and 12-bed homes.

checklist.task: Keep CPR/choking-trained staff on premises at all times
checklist.instructions: Each ACH must have at least one staff person on the premises at all times who has completed, within the last 24 months, a course on cardio-pulmonary resuscitation and choking management. Schedule recertification before the 24 months lapse and track the date for every trained staff member.

checklist.task: Retrieve the family care home staffing rules in 10A NCAC 13G
checklist.instructions: The 13G staffing section was not retrieved for this bundle, so the 6-bed FCH staffing in the model (one awake aide 24/7 plus the owner-administrator) is an operator estimate. Read the current 13G staffing rules and adjust the P&L if they require more.

checklist.task: Set wages and confirm they exceed the minimum wage
checklist.instructions: NC's minimum wage is $7.25/hour (secondary source citing NCDOL), with no local minimum and no scheduled increase (secondary). The model uses the NC median nursing assistant wage of $18.49/hour (May 2025 BLS OEWS via a secondary site) and a median LPN annual wage of $63,270. Cooks, housekeeping and activities use Raleigh-Cary metro group means ($16.61, $18.92 and $19.29/hour). Check local job postings and adjust wages for your area.
checklist.cite: NCDOL via Recording Law; BLS OEWS May 2025

checklist.task: Contract an LVN/RN nurse consultant
checklist.instructions: The models carry nurse-consultant hours (4 hrs/week for the 6-bed home up to 16 hrs/week for the 20-bed home) at $30.42/hour. The hours are operator estimates, not rule minimums. Confirm with ACLS what nursing oversight your resident mix and any medication administration require.

checklist.task: Plan staff screening, personnel files and orientation
checklist.instructions: Read the personnel, health-screening and training sections of 10A NCAC 13F or 13G for your category and build the personnel file checklist from them. Only the administrator background check, CPR/choking training and manager CE were verified in this research. The model carries $150/month for training, CE, CPR and background checks as an operator estimate.

checklist.task: Buy care-documentation/eMAR software and set up recordkeeping
checklist.instructions: The model carries $250/month for eMAR and care documentation as an operator estimate. Get vendor quotes. Whether EVV applies to your home is a separate question (see Phase 8).

checklist.task: Set up food service, laundry, activities and transportation
checklist.instructions: The model carries food at $330 per resident per month, per-resident utilities at $25, supplies at $60, activities at $20 and $250/month for a vehicle. All are operator estimates. Confirm local sanitation requirements with the county environmental health office, since sanitation approval is part of the ACH application.

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Contact county DSS about State/County Special Assistance and agree to the state rate
checklist.instructions: SA eligibility is determined through the county DSS. The facility must agree to accept the state rate for SA residents. 2026 maximums: $1,397/month in a regular ACH (secondary guide) and $1,792/month in a special care unit. The resident keeps a $70 personal needs allowance. SA is funded 50% by counties and 50% by the state, and SA recipients are automatically eligible for Medicaid. The ACH-specific official SA rate table was not retrieved, so confirm the $1,397 figure with your county DSS.
checklist.cite: NC DHHS SA ACH page; SA Manual rev. June 2026; SA SCU brochure 2026

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Understand how Medicaid fits with SA in an ACH
checklist.instructions: Medicaid can help pay for the care a resident receives in a licensed ACH but never pays room and board; SA is the channel for room and board (per a secondary guide). How ACH residents' personal care services are billed (code, modifier or per-diem arrangement) was not confirmed, so the P&L does not count Medicaid PCS as revenue. Ask NC Medicaid and your county DSS before relying on it.
checklist.cite: Mirador Living (citing NCDHHS manuals); NC Medicaid PCS update

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Track the Medicaid Personal Care Services (PCS) rate increase
checklist.instructions: Effective August 1, 2026, NC Medicaid raised State Plan PCS rates 18%: HCPCS 99509 with HA/HB modifiers went from $5.96 to $7.03 per unit. For other 99509 modifiers (HC, HH, HI, HQ, SC, TT) the daily per diem is the fee schedule rate times the beneficiary's pre-approved units. Standard and Tailored Plans have 45 calendar days to load the rates plus 30 days to reprocess claims. One plan reported billing at $7.03 could begin on 8/4/2026. Check the fee schedule portal at ncdhhs.servicenowservices.com/fee_schedules.

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Decide whether to enroll in NC Medicaid through NCTracks and budget the fees
checklist.instructions: NC charges a $100 Medicaid provider application fee on enrollment, re-enrollment and revalidation. The federal institutional provider application fee for applications submitted January 1 – December 31, 2026 is $750. Which fees apply to an ACH depends on provider type and was not confirmed. A vendor guide mentions a 12-month 'lite' enrollment option, which is not verified on an official page. Confirm the provider type and fees on NCTracks before applying.
checklist.cite: NCTracks; Federal Register CY2026 fee notice

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Confirm whether EVV applies to your home
checklist.instructions: NC Medicaid's EVV requirement covers in-home personal care services under the state plan, 1915(c) waivers and 1115 programs. A vendor page says EVV is not required for adult care homes, but that is not confirmed on NC Medicaid pages. Ask NC Medicaid in writing before buying EVV software.
checklist.cite: NC Medicaid EVV FAQ; Alora Health (vendor)

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Do not plan on CAP/DA as a payer for your residents
checklist.instructions: CAP/DA is a 1915(c) home- and community-based waiver, and a secondary source says participants cannot reside in an adult care home or a family care home. The waiver began placing applicants on a waitlist on February 16, 2024. Treat CAP/DA as a service for people living at home, not as ACH revenue.
checklist.cite: NC Medicaid CAP/DA policy; Medicaid Planning Assistance

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Set your private-pay rate from local comparables
checklist.instructions: The CareScout 2025 NC median for assisted living is about $6,496/month ($77,955/yr), from provider-reported rates collected July–November 2025 (secondary summary). It measures a private one-bedroom in an assisted living community, so it may overstate a shared-room home. The national median is $6,200/month. An older Genworth 2024 figure of $5,769 is a different survey year and should not be mixed in. Call at least five local homes, then re-run the P&L at your price.
checklist.cite: CareScout 2025 via Brevy; Buddy Insurance; ElderLife Financial

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Prepare the Adult Care Cost Report if you serve SA residents or are an exempt facility
checklist.instructions: The next Adult Care Cost Report for Special Assistance and exempt facilities is due September 30, 2027. Under S.L. 2026-41 (Senate Bill 257, Sec. 9F.2(a)), for facilities with 7 or more beds an AUP is no longer required with the cost report beginning on or after July 1, 2026. Confirm with the Office of the Controller whether your home must file and set up your books to support the report.
checklist.cite: NC DHHS Office of the Controller — Adult Care Facilities; S.L. 2026-41

checklist.phase: PHASE 8 — PAYERS: SPECIAL ASSISTANCE, MEDICAID & PRICING
checklist.task: Write resident admission agreements that reflect the SA and private-pay rules
checklist.instructions: Have your attorney draft agreements for private-pay and SA residents. For SA residents the facility must accept the state rate, and the resident keeps a $70 personal needs allowance. Do not charge SA residents above the state maximum. Read the admission and discharge sections of 10A NCAC 13F or 13G for required contents; those sections were not retrieved for this bundle.
checklist.cite: NC DHHS SA ACH page; 10A NCAC 13F / 13G

checklist.task: Register with NC Division of Employment Security (DES) for unemployment insurance
checklist.instructions: For 2026, the new-employer UI rate is 1% on a taxable wage base of $34,200 per employee. Experienced-employer rates range from 0.06% to 5.76% with a 1.9% base rate used in the formula. Register through the DES employer portal before your first payroll.

checklist.task: Set up payroll, withholding and federal payroll tax deposits
checklist.instructions: Use a payroll service (the model carries $400/month for accounting, payroll and legal as an operator estimate). The model assumes payroll taxes of 9% of wages: federal employer FICA of 7.65%, which was not in the sources retrieved so verify it, plus NC unemployment tax.

checklist.task: Obtain workers' compensation coverage
checklist.instructions: A secondary source says NC requires most businesses with three or more employees to carry workers' compensation. Employers buy on the private market or, if declined, through the assigned-risk plan run by the North Carolina Rate Bureau (NCRB). NCRB's loss costs fell an average of 7.8% effective April 1, 2026, and a further filing is approved effective April 1, 2027. The model's 4% of payroll is an operator estimate; get quotes using the correct class code for your operation.

checklist.task: Get liability, property and auto insurance quotes
checklist.instructions: No insurance or bond minimum for ACHs or FCHs was found in the DHSR pages or rules reviewed. Landlords, lenders and payers usually require coverage anyway. The model carries $80 per resident per month for general and professional liability as an operator estimate. Ask for quotes covering abuse and neglect liability, property, auto (if you transport residents) and any umbrella coverage.

checklist.task: Check E-Verify obligations
checklist.instructions: A secondary payroll guide says E-Verify is mandatory in NC at 25 or more employees. Confirm the current threshold with NC DOL or your attorney, and enroll if you reach it. The 20-bed model's staff count may approach the threshold.

checklist.task: Budget the recurring licensing and entity fees in your P&L
checklist.instructions: ACH renewal is $360 plus $17.50 per bed per year, invoiced by ACLS (12 beds = $570, 20 beds = $710). FCH renewal is $315 per year. Administrator renewal is $30 every cycle. The LLC annual report is $200 paper or $203 online. Confirm these match the model's monthly lines.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS License an ACH; DHSR ACLS License an FCH

checklist.task: Build referral relationships before opening
checklist.instructions: Referral-source shares for NC adult care homes are not published, so build your own pipeline. Contact county DSS adult services, hospital discharge planners, skilled nursing social workers, home care agencies and local aging organizations. County DSS also monitors facilities in its county, so a good relationship with them helps.

checklist.task: Plan the census ramp and fund the cash reserve
checklist.instructions: The model ramps from 1–3 residents at opening and adds 1–2 per month. At the default 88% occupancy the 12-bed ACH's first profit month is month 5 and the 20-bed 75/25 ACH's is month 8. Cash needed in the model ranges from about $92,806 (6-bed FCH, private pay) to $372,475 (20-bed ACH, 75/25 mix). Hold the working-capital reserve in the bank before you open, because occupancy in NC homes was not found in the sources and could run lower.

checklist.task: Prepare for county DSS monitoring and DHSR surveys
checklist.instructions: County social services agencies work with DHSR to monitor adult care facilities in their counties at least quarterly. Keep staffing schedules, CPR/choking training records, manager CE records, resident records and fire/safety logs ready for inspection at any time.
checklist.cite: DHSR ACLS Overview of Adult Care Home Regulation

checklist.task: File the annual license renewal on time
checklist.instructions: The licensee files a license renewal application annually on a calendar-year basis, with the nonrefundable annual fee. ACLS issued Provider Memo P0050 (July 23, 2025) on information required for the 2026 renewal application; watch the Announcements page for the next cycle's memo.

checklist.task: Know your notice duties if you sell or close
checklist.instructions: A licensee selling a home must give written notice to DHSR, county DSS and residents at least 30 days before the change of licensee. A licensee closing a home must notify DHSR, county DSS and residents at least 30 days before the planned closing.

checklist.task: Monitor Senate Bill 863 (streamlining ACH inspections)
checklist.instructions: A 2025-session bill titled 'An Act to Streamline the Inspection Process for Adult Care Homes' has a text version dated April 29, 2026. Its enactment status was not verified. Check ncleg.gov before you plan around any change to the inspection process.

checklist.task: Watch the respite-care rule change under G.S. 131D-6.1
checklist.instructions: Under a 2026 law effective July 1, 2026, the Medical Care Commission is directed to amend rules on respite care in adult care homes and family care homes as needed. If you want to offer respite stays, check for amended rules before pricing them.

checklist.task: Review the N.C. Star Rated Certificate Program rule changes
checklist.instructions: DHSR announced rule changes for the N.C. Star Rated Certificate Program effective August 1, 2025. Read the announcement and the current rule so you know how your home will be rated.

checklist.task: Recheck every quote and fee on the live official pages before you file
checklist.instructions: Several quotes in this research came from search-result excerpts, and fees such as the ACH initial fee are in conflict. Before paying any fee or relying on any rule, confirm it on the live DHSR, NCTracks and NC Medicaid pages or by calling ACLS at 919-855-3765.
